regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Definitive treatment of locally advanced cervical cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Document FIGO 2014 stage, no prior definitive therapy, ECOG 0–1 (ECOG 2 by consultant discretion) and organ reserve. Distinguish the concurrent and continuation periods from CPS-selected treatment of recurrent disease. Coordinate external-beam radiation followed by brachytherapy. If the radiation fraction is cancelled, defer cisplatin and assess pembrolizumab separately. Pembrolizumab 200 mg day 1 q21 days in cycles 1–5, followed by 400 mg day 1 q42 days for cycles 6–20. In cycles 1–2, cisplatin 40 mg/m² accompanies only the scheduled radiation visits.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Definitive treatment of locally advanced cervical cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Blocks a signal that normally slows immune cells. This can help them attack the cancer. The same response can inflame healthy organs. Attaches to DNA so cells struggle to copy and repair it. During radiotherapy this can increase damage to the cancer cells.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cycles 1–5 last 21 days. Cisplatin is planned weekly for five doses in cycles 1–2, with a possible sixth dose. Pembrolizumab continues alone from cycle 3 and changes to every 42 days for cycles 6–20. Treatment can end earlier and lasts up to 24 months. When both drugs are due, pembrolizumab is infused over 30 minutes before cisplatin over 60 minutes. IV fluids protect the kidneys. Radiation follows cisplatin that day. External-beam radiation and the later internal treatment (brachytherapy) use a separately booked calendar.
key_points: Adults with FIGO 2014 stage III–IVA cervical cancer who have not had definitive treatment. PD-L1 testing is not required for this indication.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Confirm high-grade serous histology, platinum resistance, ECOG 0–2 and 1–3 prior systemic regimens. Validated FRα IHC must show moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining in ≥75% of viable tumour cells. NCCP specifies the VENTANA FOLR1 RxDx assay. Use 6 mg/kg adjusted ideal body weight, q21 days. Baseline slit lamp and acuity are required. Use the worst affected eye for dose decisions. Document pre-existing corneal disease, neuropathy or noninfectious pneumonitis. Initial infusion 1 mg/min for 30 minutes, then if tolerated 3 mg/min for 30 minutes and up to 5 mg/min. Later infusions may use the highest tolerated rate. Prepare and flush in glucose 5%, using a PES filter. Consider pneumonitis with new pulmonary symptoms.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: An antibody recognises folate receptor alpha on some cancer cells and carries a medicine inside them that interferes with cell division.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: One infusion on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team reviews benefit and side effects each cycle. Treatment continues until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable. You receive medicines to reduce sickness and infusion reactions before the drip. The first infusion starts slowly and may speed up in steps while the nurse checks you. The dose is based on height and weight. Subsequent infusions may use the rate you previously tolerated.
key_points: For adults whose high-grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer resists platinum, expresses folate receptor alpha at the required level and has had one to three prior systemic regimens.

context_regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Confirm small-cell cervical histology and radiation field in multidisciplinary review. Default etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–3 and cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1, q21 days ×4. The alternate schedule uses etoposide 100 mg/m² IV day 1 then 100 mg/m² orally twice daily on days 2–3. NCCP permits consultant-selected q28 days, cisplatin 25 mg/m² across days 1–3, or day-1 carboplatin AUC 5 if cisplatin toxicity, poor function or age over 75 warrants substitution. If etoposide is oral on day 1 at consultant discretion, separately ensure prehydration. Explain the unlicensed indication in Ireland and obtain informed consent under local policy. Confirm acknowledgment by the hospital Drugs and Therapeutics Committee or equivalent. Check suitability for radiotherapy and ECOG 0–2, renal clearance, hearing and neuropathy. NCCP excludes cisplatin at CrCl below 60 mL/min, pre-existing grade ≥2 neuropathy or significant hearing impairment/tinnitus.
context_regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Blocks an enzyme that cells need to repair DNA while dividing. Rapidly dividing blood and hair cells can be affected too. Attaches to DNA so cells struggle to copy and repair it. During radiotherapy this can increase damage to the cancer cells.
context_regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Usually four 21-day cycles. Cisplatin is normally given on day 1 and etoposide on days 1–3. The consultant can select a 28-day interval. Radiation usually starts with cycle 1 but can start later for clinical reasons. On the usual day 1, etoposide runs into a vein over about an hour and is followed by cisplatin over about an hour, with protective fluids. On days 2–3, etoposide is either infused or prescribed as capsules twice daily. The written plan states which route and whether cisplatin is split across three days.
key_points: This pathway covers the cervical small-cell neuroendocrine cancer indication. The specialist team confirms the pathology, stage and local radiation plan.

Five-year failure-free survival was 42.9% versus 11.8% in this selected subgroup. The observational association cannot establish treatment causality or the optimal number of cycles.

treatment_rationale.summary: Confirm small-cell cervical histology and radiation field in multidisciplinary review. context_regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Document primary site, intent and the specific indication (a–c adjuvant, d–f first-line unresectable stage III–IV, g–i platinum-sensitive recurrence). Give single-agent carboplatin AUC 4–6 day 1 every 28 days. Use Calvert dosing with GFR in mL/min, capped at 125 mL/min for this calculation. Prefer measured GFR where estimated values may mislead. Review baseline and prior nadirs, cumulative platinum exposure and hypersensitivity. NCCP describes treatment to progression or unacceptable toxicity; document a case-specific course and review date. In initial cycles the source requests FBC on days 13–15 and 21 to establish nadir. ECOG 0–2; a performance status of 3 is permitted when due to advanced ovarian, peritoneal or tube cancer. Progression during platinum therapy excludes this regimen. A previous platinum reaction requires specialist review and any exceptional desensitisation follows hospital policy. Table 1 gives full dose for ANC ≥1 × 10⁹/L AND platelets ≥100 × 10⁹/L. If either is below its threshold, delay one week or until recovery. Individual thresholds can be higher, especially with ECOG 2–3. Check all other eligibility and toxicity findings.

Blood checks and anti-sickness medicine add time to the visit. The team works out your dose from kidney function and a prescribed target exposure.

evidence_at_a_glance.population: EWOC-1 randomised 120 vulnerable women aged 70 or older with newly diagnosed stage III–IV ovarian cancer. The separate AGO-OVAR trial enrolled 356 patients with platinum-sensitive recurrence.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: EWOC-1 compared three-weekly carboplatin alone with two carboplatin/paclitaxel schedules. AGO-OVAR compared carboplatin alone with gemcitabine plus carboplatin in recurrence.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Document primary site, intent and the specific indication (a–c adjuvant, d–f first-line unresectable stage III–IV, g–i platinum-sensitive recurrence). Give single-agent carboplatin AUC 4–6 day 1 every 21 days. Use Calvert dosing with GFR in mL/min, capped at 125 mL/min for this calculation. Prefer measured GFR where estimated values may mislead. Review baseline and prior nadirs, cumulative platinum exposure and hypersensitivity. NCCP describes treatment to progression or unacceptable toxicity; document a case-specific course and review date. The gynaecology schedule has no concurrent radiation or fixed three-cycle course. ECOG 0–2; a performance status of 3 is permitted when due to advanced ovarian, peritoneal or tube cancer. Progression during platinum therapy excludes this regimen. A previous platinum reaction requires specialist review and any exceptional desensitisation follows hospital policy. Table 1 gives full dose for ANC ≥1 × 10⁹/L AND platelets ≥100 × 10⁹/L. If either is below its threshold, delay one week or until recovery. Individual thresholds can be higher, especially with ECOG 2–3. Check all other eligibility and toxicity findings.
limitations: The studies involve different settings and do not compare 21-day with 28-day administration. Neither provides an individual prognosis. EWOC-1 was stopped early in a selected vulnerable population; age alone does not establish that combination treatment is unsuitable.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Low platelets and bleeding, Low white cells and infection, Anaemia, Nausea and vomiting, Platinum hypersensitivity

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: In EWOC-1, six cycles were completed by 48% with three-weekly carboplatin alone versus 65% with the three-weekly doublet. In recurrent disease, median progression-free survival was 5.8 months with carboplatin alone versus 8.6 with gemcitabine/carboplatin.

evidence_audit.coverage_summary: In EWOC-1, six cycles were completed by 48% with three-weekly carboplatin alone versus 65% with the three-weekly doublet. In recurrent disease, median progression-free survival was 5.8 months with carboplatin alone versus 8.6 with gemcitabine/carboplatin.
remaining_uncertainties: The studies involve different settings and do not compare 21-day with 28-day administration. Neither provides an individual prognosis. EWOC-1 was stopped early in a selected vulnerable population; age alone does not establish that combination treatment is unsuitable.
covered_contexts: Three groups are covered for epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer: after surgery when combination chemotherapy is unsuitable; first treatment of stage III–IV disease when surgery is infeasible and combination treatment unsuitable; or recurrence that remains sensitive to platinum.

evidence_records.publication_title: EMA Keytruda product information · KEYNOTE-A18, Table 51
evidence_records.evidence_context: 601 participants with FIGO 2014 stage III–IVA in the EMA subgroup analysis of the broader 1,060-participant randomised phase III trial.
key_findings: At median follow-up of 26.6 months in the stage III–IVA subgroup, the overall-survival HR was 0.57 (95% CI 0.39–0.83) and the progression-free survival HR was 0.57 (0.43–0.76). These are the subgroup estimates reported in EMA Table 51.
evidence_records.limitations: Subgroup findings are exploratory. The overall trial also included earlier node-positive stages. It did not test pembrolizumab alone against chemoradiotherapy or directly compare induction chemotherapy.

evidence_records.evidence_context: 453 patients with platinum-resistant high-grade serous disease, high FRα expression and one to three previous treatment regimens.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 5.62 versus 3.98 months. Median overall survival was 16.46 versus 12.75 months (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.50–0.89). Objective responses occurred in 42.3% versus 15.9%.
evidence_records.limitations: Randomised open-label trial in a biomarker-selected population. These group estimates cannot predict individual benefit or be applied to FRα-low, platinum-sensitive or differently pretreated disease.
